s: A company runs a custom inventory application on Oracle Database Enterprise Edition on premises. The application uses standard SQL, a few dozen PL/SQL stored procedures, and no Oracle-specific options. The Oracle support renewal is due in 9 months. The company wants to eliminate commercial database license costs while keeping changes to the application tier to a minimum. Which migration approach should a solutions architect recommend?
o: Rehost the Oracle database server to Amazon EC2 by using AWS Application Migration Service.
Migrate the database to Amazon RDS for Oracle by using the License Included model for Enterprise Edition.

Convert the schema and stored procedures to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL by using DMS Schema Conversion, migrate the data with AWS DMS using full load and change data capture, and update the application's connection settings and any incompatible SQL.
Migrate the database to Amazon RDS Custom for Oracle with bring your own license.

w.y: Only a move to an open-source-compatible engine eliminates commercial database license costs. With standard SQL and few stored procedures, DMS Schema Conversion can convert the schema and code to Aurora PostgreSQL and AWS DMS can move the data with change data capture, limiting application changes to connection settings and minor SQL fixes.

o.A: Keeps Oracle Enterprise Edition licenses and support costs.
o.B: License Included is not offered for Oracle Enterprise Edition, and any RDS for Oracle option still carries Oracle license cost.
o.C: Correct: removes Oracle licensing with limited application changes.
o.D: Still requires the Oracle licenses the company wants to eliminate.
